title: Protocol to quantify palmitoylation of cysteines in budding yeast
protocol: Add 600 μL of yeast lysis buffer to the yeast pellet.
Add 100 μL of 0.5 mm glass beads to the mixture.
Shake with a high-throughput tissue grinder at 60 Hz for 60 seconds, then incubate on ice for 5 minutes; repeat this process 6 times in total.
Centrifuge the sample at 5000 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Collect the supernatant and transfer it to a new 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Quantify protein concentrations of the supernatant using a bicinchoninic acid (BCA) kit from Sigma.
Dilute one milligram of protein supernatant with lysis buffer to reach a total volume of 600 μL.
Add Triton X-100 at a final concentration by adding 6 μL of 100% Triton X-100 into the cell lysates.
Add final 25 mM N-ethylmaleimide (NEM) to the samples.
Incubate the protein samples at 4°C for 30 minutes with gentle full-angle rotation.
Store one tube from each sample at –80°C as a backup.
Transfer 1 mg of protein, diluted in LB buffer (with PI) to a final volume of 1 mL, into larger polypropylene centrifuge tubes.
Add 4 mL of methanol to the tubes and vortex thoroughly.
Add 1.5 mL of chloroform to the tubes and vortex thoroughly.
Add 3 mL of distilled H2O to the tubes and vortex thoroughly.
Place the tubes at 4°C for 20 min.
Centrifuge (12,000×g, 10 min, 4°C) to separate the phases.
Discard the top phase using Pasteur pipettes carefully.
Add 3 mL methanol followed by gentle up and down mixing.
Centrifuge (3,000×g, 10 min, 4°C).
Remove the supernatant with a Pasteur pipette.
Add methanol to yeast cell lysates and vortex thoroughly.
Add chloroform to the mixture and vortex thoroughly.
Add distilled H2O to the tubes and vortex thoroughly.
Centrifuge the samples at 12,000×g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard the top phase using Pasteur pipettes.
Add methanol again followed by gentle up and down mixing.
Centrifuge at 3,000×g for 10 min at 4°C to pellet protein precipitates.
Discard the supernatant with a Pasteur pipette.
Air dry the protein pellets.
Dissolve the protein in 450 μL SB buffer.
Incubate the dissolved protein at 37°C for 20–30 minutes.
Divide protein samples into two equal aliquots, retaining 50 μL for western blotting.
Mix one aliquot (200 μL) with 800 μL of With-HA buffer and incubate at 25°C for 1–2 hours by gentle mixing.
Mix the other aliquot (200 μL) with 800 μL of Without-HA buffer and incubate at 25°C for 1–2 hours by gentle mixing.
Use chloroform and methanol assays to precipitate proteins as described in steps 4-5.
Dissolve protein precipitates in 100 μL TB buffer.
Incubate at 37°C for 10 minutes.
Dilute with 900 μL LB buffer.
Use the CM assay to precipitate proteins if unreacted biotin is present, repeating up to three times if necessary.
Add 30 μL of streptavidin-agarose beads to the samples.
Incubate at 4°C for 1–2 hours.
Wash streptavidin-agarose beads with washing buffer five times.
Add 60–80 μL Elution buffer to the beads.
Boil the beads for 5 minutes as pulldown samples.
Load 10 μL of input and pulldown samples into SDS-PAGE gels.
Proceed with western blotting using anti-HA antibody.
